headline: SVG Sprite Generator simplifies embedding multiple images in one file
summary: A new tool combines images into a single SVG and provides HTML/CSS code for individual embedding, offering an alternative to traditional CSS background sprites.
details: A developer has created a web-based generator to simplify the process of using SVG sprites, which allows multiple images to be stored within a single SVG file and embedded individually.
This technique uses a standard tag format, such as sprite.svg#icon, eliminating the need for complex background-position management often associated with CSS background sprites.
The SVG Sprite Generator tool not only combines images but also provides the necessary HTML and CSS code, making it easier for developers to implement this efficient image embedding method.
The creator is seeking feedback on the tool, particularly regarding any limitations or issues users might encounter, aiming to refine the existing technique and make it more accessible.

headline: ChatGPT now generates virtual try-on photos using uploaded images
summary: OpenAI's latest AI model allows users to upload selfies and see themselves in clothing items from product listings.
details: OpenAI has integrated a new virtual try-on feature into ChatGPT, powered by its September-released ChatGPT Images 2.5 model. Users can now upload their own photos, including selfies and full-body shots, to see how clothing items would look on them.

This feature functions within product listings in ChatGPT chats. Tapping on a clothing item and selecting 'Try on' prompts the user to upload their images. The AI then generates a virtual try-on photo, similar to a feature introduced by Google Search.

Beyond virtual try-ons, ChatGPT now also allows users to save products they are interested in to a dedicated Library within the app for later review. This expands ChatGPT's utility as a shopping assistant.

Users should be aware that, by default, uploaded images may be used for AI training unless they opt out. OpenAI has previously experimented with e-commerce features like the discontinued Instant Checkout, indicating a continued focus on integrating shopping functionalities into its AI services.
